answers.answer: Top to bottom: 1 randomly dealt card from the shuffled 4 Conflict I cards, then 5 randomly dealt from the shuffled 10 Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Shuffle each tier before dealing; return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “1 card randomly dealt…; 5 cards randomly dealt…; all 4 Conflict III cards… Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 3 troops in their garrison and the other 9 in supply; 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. VP: 1 in four-player, 0 otherwise (so 0 in three-player).
answers.evidence: Setup: “2 Agents”; “third Agent (their Swordmaster)”; score “1…in a 4-player game, otherwise…0”; 4 Influence cubes, 3 garrison troops, remaining troops in supply; “takes 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may Reveal while Agents remain. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, including during that Reveal turn, but not later in the phase after your turn is over.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal “your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Plot Intrigue may be played “during…one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.”

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up with at least one Agent icon matching the destination’s icon; select only one icon and send only one Agent from your Leader. The space must be unoccupied. Meet all space requirements and pay entry costs immediately before resolving card or space effects; if unable to pay, you cannot go there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “play one card…send one Agent”; matching icon, one icon only; space unoccupied; meet requirements and pay costs “immediately, before resolving any effects.”

answers.answer: No. You must pay Conspire’s 4-spice entry cost before resolving the card, so spice gained from that Agent box cannot fund entry when you have only 3. After paying entry cost, resolve the board-space effect, Agent box, and Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs paid “before resolving any effects”; afterward gain space, Agent box, and Influence “in any order.” Board table: Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: Maximum deployment is 5: all 3 troops recruited this turn (2 from the space plus 1 from the card) and up to 2 more from the garrison. Undeployed recruited troops stay in the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits go to the garrison and cannot normally deploy on that turn.
answers.evidence: Deploying: “any or all troops you recruited this turn… plus up to two more troops from your garrison”; recruits not deployed go to garrison. Rally Troops is explicitly “not a Combat space.”

answers.answer: In order: reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve Reveal boxes of those newly revealed cards (not Agent-turn cards); set strength; clean up. At cleanup all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn numbered steps 1–4; step 2 excludes cards played on Agent turns; step 4 puts “all the cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns)” into discard.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row is immediately refilled, and you may buy its replacement if affordable. Persuasion from multiple sources may be pooled for one card and a source may be split across different cards. Leftover Persuasion is lost. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and is not usable immediately. Its Acquire effect happens once at acquisition, not when played.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: row refills immediately; pooling/splitting allowed; Persuasion cannot be saved; acquired cards go to discard and “you don’t use them right away”; Acquire box occurs “at the moment you acquire the card.”

answers.answer: 3 troops are 6 strength and 4 revealed swords add 4, total 10. If the last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. For strength over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn: each troop = 2, each sword = 1; no troops means 0 and cannot be increased; over 20 use +20 side and restart track.

answers.answer: Players with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, beginning with the First Player and continuing clockwise. A pass does not prevent later play in the phase. Combat resolves after all players involved pass consecutively. “When you win” cards are played only after you have won and before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: First Player clockwise; each with a troop may play cards or pass; “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards only after winning.

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each receives the second reward. C and D then compete for the third reward; C gets it and D gets nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in 2–3 player games; tie for third gives nothing. Zero strength earns no reward. After rewards, troops return to supply, not garrison.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and rewards: first tie means no winner and second reward to each; in four-player play the others compete for third. Second tie gets third each; third tie nothing; 0 strength none; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: Harvesting occurs in the Agent turn when visiting a Maker space, under that space’s listed cost/effect; the base amounts are 1 spice at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin, and 3 at The Great Flat, plus any accumulated bonus spice. The Makers phase comes after Combat and adds 1 bonus spice to each of those spaces that has no Agent at that time. An Agent that moved away leaves the space empty, so bonus spice accumulates there.
answers.evidence: Board table lists Maker space costs and base gains plus bonus. Phase 4 places 1 spice on each Agent-free Maker space; clarification says if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, spice accumulates.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately: check at the end of the round during Recall. The empty Conflict Deck also triggers the end then. Endgame Intrigue cards resolve before determining the winner. Tiebreaks in order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: trigger “at the end of a round”; Endgame cards resolve first; tiebreak order lists spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence you gain 1 VP, which is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The 4-Influence track bonus is retained after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and advancing. First to 4 takes Alliance and its VP; merely tying the holder does not take it, but advancing above them transfers it.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence and Alliances: 2 VP lost below and regained; 4 bonus not returned and may be earned again; first to 4 takes Alliance; only passing by rising higher transfers it.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of those previously tied players takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses one. If you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the token; with no other player at 4+, it returns to the board and you lose its VP.
answers.evidence: Alliance section: on holder losing Influence while tied, tied player takes it (holder chooses among several); holder falling to 3 or less loses it and if nobody has 4+, return to board.

answers.answer: Discarding normally means a card from your hand and sends it to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard, or play to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card directs self-trashing. You may not reshuffle early just to inspect the top: reshuffle only when unable to draw because the deck is empty.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards and Deck exhaustion sections give these destinations, eligible zones, exceptions and no-early-reshuffle rule.

answers.answer: When anyone visits a space you control, you receive 1 Solari for Arrakeen or Carthag, or 1 spice for Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict places/replaces your Control marker there. When a matching Conflict is revealed later, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places marker; controller receives bonus whenever any player sends an Agent; on reveal of a Conflict for a space you control, may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: House Hagal setup: use an unused color; put one cube at the bottom of each Influence track and remaining cubes in supply, with no troops in its garrison; remove three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the rest, and place its deck and three Agents by supply. It has no Leader or solo difficulty rules. It never Reveals; it takes turns after each First Player Agent turn. It does not collect resources, score VP, or earn Conflict rewards, but can hold Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal section spells out setup, turn trigger, three Agents, no Reveal, no resources/VP/rewards, and ability to hold Alliances.

answers.answer: After each First Player Agent turn, Hagal reveals until it finds a card with an eligible unoccupied indicated space; if its deck is empty or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and continue. If a two-space card’s applicable option is occupied, draw another card rather than switching options. Ignore normal space costs, requirements and effects; resolve only card icons/instructions. Troop icons recruit; on Combat spaces deploy those recruits, otherwise garrison them. On any Combat space it automatically deploys up to two additional available garrison troops. Harvest Spice selects a Maker space as specified; harvested bonus spice is removed and returned to bank.
answers.evidence: Two-player Agent-turn section provides these occupied-space, reshuffle, cost/effect, troop deployment and Harvest Spice rules.

answers.answer: If Hagal has troops in the Conflict, at Combat start reveal a Hagal card (reshuffle and reveal again if needed), add its sword icons to 2 strength per troop, then humans play Combat Intrigue. Hagal gets no rank reward but occupies its rank when assigning human rewards. If it wins a space controlled by a human, remove that Control marker. Human tie for second still earns the third reward, even though ordinary third place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Hagal Combat strength procedure; “receives no reward for its rank, but it still occupies that rank”; removes human Control if it wins; general second-place tie rule.

answers.answer: At Round Start reveal the top Conflict card and each player draws 5 cards. In non-ending Recall, return Mentat to its Landsraad space, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise, and start the next round. A Sort Through the Chaos winner takes the Mentat at the start of that next round.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 and Phase 5: Conflict reveal and draw 5; Recall returns Mentat, recalls Agents, passes marker; FAQ timing for Sort Through the Chaos.

answers.answer: Bank resources are not limited; substitute if the bank runs out of water, spice, or Solari. Troop cubes differ: if your supply has no troops, you cannot recruit more until some return.
answers.evidence: Setup: tokens “are not limited; substitute if you run out.” Agent turn recruiting: if supply is out, cannot recruit until troops return.

answers.answer: Each Leader has an ability used during play as described on the Leader, and a Signet Ring ability activated when you play your Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns. Card text can override the game’s usual rules.
answers.evidence: Overview states both Leader ability timings and that “cards of any type can override the usual rules.”

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr has no Agent icon of its own specified in the board table (it is a City space), requires at least 2 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and gains one water; it is a Combat space and therefore permits deployment. You cannot enter at 1 Influence and use a card effect afterward to reach 2, because the requirement must be met to enter.
answers.evidence: Board spaces section lists City spaces, Sietch Tabr requirement/effects; Combat-space list includes it; Agent turn requires meeting space requirements before effects.

answers.answer: Combat spaces are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors, and Stillsuits. Research Station and The Great Flat are Combat spaces; Conspire is not.
answers.evidence: Complete list of Combat spaces states exactly these spaces and explicitly says Conspire is not normally a deployment space.

answers.answer: Wealth: no cost; +1 Emperor Influence and 2 Solari. Conspire: 4 spice; +1 Emperor Influence, 5 Solari, 2 troops, 1 Intrigue. Foldspace: no cost; +1 Spacing Guild Influence and acquire a Foldspace card from Reserve. Heighliner: 6 spice; +1 Spacing Guild Influence, 5 troops, 2 water. Secrets: no cost; +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw an Intrigue, and each opponent with 4+ Intrigue cards gives one at random. Selective Breeding: 2 spice; +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, trash one card to draw two. Stillsuits: no cost; +1 Fremen Influence and 1 water. Hardy Warriors: 1 water; +1 Fremen Influence and 2 troops.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists all costs and effects including Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: no cost; recruit 1 troop and draw a card; its controller gains 1 Solari. Carthag: no cost; recruit 1 troop and draw an Intrigue; controller gains 1 Solari. Research Station: 2 water; draw 3 cards. Secure Contract: no cost; gain 3 Solari. Imperial Basin: no cost; gain 1 spice plus bonus spice; controller gains 1 spice. Hagga Basin: 1 water; gain 2 spice plus bonus. The Great Flat: 2 water; gain 3 spice plus bonus.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists costs/effects and controller bonuses; Maker spaces add accumulated bonus spice.

answers.answer: Sell Melange exchanges 2 spice for 6 Solari, 3 for 8, 4 for 10, or 5 for 12. One exchange per turn. Its Agent icon is Spice Trade.
answers.evidence: Board table gives exchange rates and one exchange per turn; Agent icons section classifies Sell Melange as Spice Trade.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari and may be used once per game; placing the Councilor grants 2 Persuasion during each Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Swordmaster costs 8 Solari and may be used once per game; gain the third Agent, place it on your Leader, and have three Agents for the rest of the game, including that round.
answers.evidence: Board table: costs, once-per-game frequency and benefits/timing.

answers.answer: Hall of Oratory costs nothing, recruits one troop, and gives 1 Persuasion on your Reveal if you have an Agent there. Rally Troops costs 4 Solari and recruits four troops to your garrison (not a Combat space). Mentat costs 2 Solari and draws a card; if the Mentat is there, take it to your Leader to use as an Agent this round, returning it during Recall.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table provides these costs and effects.

answers.answer: A recalled Agent returns to your Leader and may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. It does not reopen turns after you have already Revealed.
answers.evidence: Recall effects clarification states both rules.

answers.answer: Fremen Bond works if there is at least one other Fremen card in play. Agent-turn cards and Reveal-turn cards remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed. Two Bond cards activate each other regardless of play order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond clarification states all three points.

answers.answer: A single gain-two-Influence effect cannot be split between Factions. Alliance-icon effects require that you hold that Faction’s Alliance; numeric Influence-requirement icons require at least the printed Influence in that Faction.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons clarification explicitly states these rules.

answers.answer: Intrigue cards are held face down separately from your deck; you may look at them but reveal only when played, and played cards go face up beside the Intrigue Deck after resolving. Plot cards can be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat cards only during Combat; Endgame cards only at game end. If the deck runs out, shuffle discards into a new deck. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play; they cannot be bypassed.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section gives privacy, destination, timing, reshuffle; Agent turn rules say Intrigue costs and conditions must be met.

answers.answer: Yes. A delayed Plot such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission can be played during your Agent turn; leave it face up until that Reveal turn, use its effect then, and discard it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section explicitly describes delayed Plot cards.

answers.answer: A card drawn during your Reveal must immediately be revealed and used in that turn; you cannot hold it for a later Agent turn. Cards drawn after your Reveal remain in hand for next round, in addition to drawing five at Round Start.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn step 2 states both cases.

answers.answer: Ordinary card/board effects are generally mandatory unless they say “may,” are an optional arrow, or use optional black-X trash; a non-arrow self-trash instruction is mandatory. An ordinary card’s optional arrow payment/effect may be declined, but a board entry cost must be paid to enter, and Intrigue costs/conditions must be met to play. An optional arrow effect can be paid and resolved only once, not repeated by paying again.
answers.evidence: Agent turn arrow/effect rules give optionality, required costs, and one-time limit.

answers.answer: Play Bindu Suspension at the start of your Agent turn before anything else; draw a card, then immediately end your turn.
answers.evidence: Rulebook clarifications: Bindu Suspension.

answers.answer: No. Calculated Hire can take the Mentat only from its starting position in the Landsraad, not from another player or a board space where deployed. For Sort Through the Chaos, take the Mentat at the start of the next round.
answers.evidence: Mentat and FAQ clarifications specify both.

answers.answer: Kwisatz Haderach permits an Agent turn with no unused Agents by sending an Agent already on a board space, including back to that same space. It cannot reuse High Council or Swordmaster, and cannot overcome The Voice.
answers.evidence: Kwisatz Haderach clarification gives these restrictions and permission.

answers.answer: The Voice marks the chosen space with one of your available Control markers; remove that marker on your next turn. It stops opponents, including via Kwisatz Haderach, from sending Agents there for one turn.
answers.evidence: The Voice clarification states timing, target and component.

answers.answer: Test of Humanity: opponents choose in order starting from your left and going clockwise; each must choose an action they can actually perform. If an opponent discards, that opponent chooses the card; it is not random. The summary gives no rule for Reverend Mother Mohiam’s card-discard choice or ordering, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Rulebook clarifications explicitly cover Test of Humanity only: clockwise from your left; feasible choices; discarding opponent chooses. No Mohiam ruling appears in the summary.

answers.answer: After setup and before round 1, Baron secretly chooses two of the four tokens, places them Faction-side down on the Leader, and returns the other two unseen. They are revealed later for the reward, only once per game. The summary does not specify further timing/conditions for revealing individual tokens.
answers.evidence: Baron clarification: “secretly choose two… place them Faction-side down… reveal later as described… only once per game”; the detailed reveal trigger is not given.

answers.answer: Demand Respect can be funded with spice received for winning a Conflict that rewards spice; To the Victor… can also fund it. A win-trigger Intrigue drawn as a victory reward may be played immediately. A win-trigger card cannot be played on a first-place tie because nobody won.
answers.evidence: Clarifications for Demand Respect and Combat ties state these outcomes.

answers.answer: Yes, “any number” can be zero. A retreated troop moves from the Conflict to your garrison; a lost troop returns to your supply.
answers.evidence: Losing vs. retreating troops clarification.

answers.answer: Assassination Mission does not self-trash to gain its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws an Intrigue only when using its own self-trash effect, not if another effect trashes it.
answers.evidence: FAQ clarifications explicitly state both.

answers.answer: Yes, keep the VP gained for acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if it is later trashed. Guild Bankers’ discount applies to each copy acquired that turn.
answers.evidence: FAQ clarification for The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers.

answers.answer: Count your The Spice Must Flow cards in your deck and discard pile. For the second requirement, compare against each opponent separately; if any one has at least as many as you, you fail that requirement.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification.

answers.answer: Count Ilban’s Ruthless Negotiator triggers only for paying a board space’s printed Solari cost, not a card ability costing Solari. Ariana’s Spice Addict is mandatory and applies only to spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice from other sources.
answers.evidence: FAQ clarifications for both Leaders.

answers.answer: Original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin, and 3 at The Great Flat; bonus spice is additional, not base. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from this round’s Agent turns and the current Reveal turn, for 2 Persuasion each.
answers.evidence: Carryall / Liet Kynes clarification.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the set-aside card. You may acquire it by another effect, but the 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: Helena Richese — Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but does not require a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter’s Agent box has no effect on an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Double Cross / Gun Thopter clarification.

answers.answer: Shifting Allegiances may lose and gain Influence in the same Faction for a net gain of one, but you must actually pay the loss; a Faction where you have zero cannot pay it. Each track has six spaces; 3 Influence is immediately above the 2-Influence VP space.
answers.evidence: Shifting Allegiances and Faction Influence clarifications.

answers.answer: Recruitment Mission’s destination choice applies only to acquisitions during that Reveal turn, not Agent-turn acquisitions. For multiple cards acquired during Reveal, choose independently for each whether it goes on top of your deck or into discard.
answers.evidence: Recruitment Mission clarification.

answers.answer: Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. A card drawn during Reveal must immediately be revealed and used during that Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Refocus / Poison Snooper clarification.

answers.answer: Missionaria Protectiva belongs to the Bene Gesserit Faction. After replacing first-printing misprints, include only two copies in the Imperium deck.
answers.evidence: Missionaria Protectiva erratum.

answers.answer: Yes. A player can score above 12 VP; the printed Score track end is not a limit.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory section: “You can score above 12 VP; the end of the printed Score track is not a limit.”

answers.answer: Rivals are affected by effects targeting opponents or players if they have the specified resources. They do not gain Influence-track bonuses and Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play.
answers.evidence: House Hagal section explicitly gives these rules.

answers.answer: House Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn, not after the second human’s turns or after a Reveal. Its turn count follows the First Player’s actual Agent turns and Hagal’s remaining Agents, up to three; Swordmaster can mean an additional First Player Agent turn, but there is no fixed two-turn cap. Early Reveal or recall/temporary Mentat can also alter the count.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns section gives timing, maximum three and explains Swordmaster example/no fixed two-turn limit.

answers.answer: No. Ordinary Reveal Persuasion cannot buy Foldspace from the Reserve; acquiring Foldspace requires an acquire-Foldspace icon (normally from visiting Foldspace).
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards section: Foldspace requires an acquire-Foldspace icon and cannot be bought with Persuasion.

answers.answer: You retain City and Fremen. Dispatch an Envoy adds only missing Faction icons and never duplicates an existing icon, so you do not get a second Fremen icon.
answers.evidence: Dispatch an Envoy clarification.

answers.answer: Yes. Troops recruited that turn from any source, including Plot Intrigue cards, may deploy when you send an Agent to a Combat space, plus up to two more from your garrison. You cannot re-recruit garrison troops to bypass the two-additional limit.
answers.evidence: Deploying section says recruits from any source, including Intrigue cards, plus up to two garrison troops; cannot re-recruit to evade limit.

answers.answer: Draw the one card remaining. When another draw is required and the deck is empty, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing until you have three. Cards still face up in play are not in the discard pile and do not join that shuffle; they go to discard at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: Deck exhaustion: reshuffle when unable to draw, then continue. Reveal cleanup puts cards in play into discard only at cleanup.

answers.answer: Set Mentat on its side in its space and Alliance tokens on their track markers. Shuffle Intrigue and place face down; shuffle Imperium and deal five face-up Row cards; place the three Reserve stacks. Each human chooses/receives a Leader, puts two Agents on it and the third by the board, shuffles the 10-card starting deck, places score at 1 in 4-player or 0 otherwise, Combat at 0, one cube at bottom of each Faction track, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in visible supply, and takes one water. Randomly choose the First Player.
answers.evidence: Setup section lists these setup steps and starting deck/components.

answers.answer: Unused player components/supply are placed in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards remain face down and may be looked at by their owner; their faces are revealed only when played, so they are not public.
answers.evidence: Setup says remaining components/supply in clear view. Intrigue section says keep face down, may look at any time, reveal only when played.

answers.answer: You may acquire cards before, between, or after resolving Reveal effects; you do not have to finish all Reveal effects first.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn explicitly permits Persuasion acquisitions “before, between, or after” Reveal effects.

answers.answer: City: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station. Landsraad: High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops, Mentat. Spice Trade: Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Secure Contract, Sell Melange.
answers.evidence: Agent icons section lists the exact City, Spice Trade and Landsraad spaces.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn, then players proceed clockwise one turn at a time. On each turn a player chooses an Agent or Reveal turn; Agent turns continue until a player chooses to Reveal or has no Agents. After a Reveal, that player is skipped; the phase ends once everyone has Revealed.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 Player Turns section.

answers.answer: With strengths 8, 6 and 4, the 8-strength player wins and receives the top reward, 6 gets second, and 4 gets no reward in a three-player game. In four players only, an ordinary third-place finisher gets the third reward.
answers.evidence: Combat resolution: top and second rewards; ordinary third reward only in a four-player game; ties section says 0 strength gets none, though this case is positive 4 and ordinary third in three players has no reward.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, reveal Hagal’s combat-bonus card first (reshuffling and revealing again if needed); then humans play Combat Intrigue in First Player order, clockwise. If Hagal has no troop in the Conflict, it does not get the combat-bonus reveal.
answers.evidence: Hagal Combat strength procedure occurs at start; humans play after. It applies “if House Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict.”

answers.answer: Corner the Market scores independently: 1 VP for having at least two The Spice Must Flow cards, and another 1 VP for having more than each opponent (compare separately; any opponent with as many or more prevents this second point). Each condition scores on its own, so either can earn 1 VP and both earn 2.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification.

answers.answer: Yes. Sardaukar Legion’s Reveal box can deploy up to three troops from your garrison. Resolve it during Reveal effects before setting strength, so the deployed troops count immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn exception explicitly names Sardaukar Legion and timing.

answers.answer: Landsraad Popularity reduces by 1 Solari the entry cost of a Landsraad (green) space when Leto sends an Agent there; apply before payment. Prudent Diplomacy optionally costs 1 spice for 1 Influence in a Faction where an opponent has more Influence than Leto. A Faction with no opponent ahead is not eligible.
answers.evidence: Duke Leto FAQ clarification.

answers.answer: Harvest Spice selects the Maker space with the most bonus spice; ties are broken by total spice (base plus bonus). If no Maker space has bonus spice, reveal another Hagal card. The harvested bonus spice is removed and returned to the bank; Hagal does not keep resources.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Harvest Spice ruling.

answers.answer: Machinations’ first-place “Choose two” means choose two different Faction gain-one icons and gain 1 Influence in each; you cannot place both in one Faction. This is specifically different from a generic gain-two-Influence effect, which cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons clarification explicitly distinguishes Machinations: choose two different Factions.

answers.answer: No. Master Tactician offers 3 swords OR retreat up to 3 troops, so one play gives only one option. If retreating, move those troops from the Conflict to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Intrigue example: “3 swords OR retreat up to 3 troops” and Losing vs. retreating clarification says retreat to garrison.
